narrativeProgression.description: Interview with the author about his book on Charles Manson.
The interviewer mentions the book focuses on Charles Manson.
Donal Barty asks what inspired Marlin Marynick to write the book.
Marlin Marynick explains he's a psychiatric nurse and had the opportunity to meet Manson.
Marlin Marynick shares that the book explores his motivations for wanting to meet Manson.
Marlin Marynick describes the book as complex and states he included important people from Manson's life.
Marlin Marynick mentions Manson's dialogue contributes to the core of the book.
Donal Barty asks what makes this book different from other Manson books.
Marlin Marynick explains Manson's media silence for the past 20 years makes this book a candid and authentic look at him.
Marlin Marynick states that Manson is the most complex person he's ever met.
Donal Barty asks if Manson has seen or read the book.
Marlin Marynick confirms Manson has read the book and approves of the content.
Marlin Marynick discusses the challenges of communication with Manson due to his prison restrictions.
Marlin Marynick shares feedback from people who know Manson and think it's the most honest book about him.
Marlin Marynick clarifies he's not just promoting his book, but emphasizes his attempt to be authentic.
Marlin Marynick talks about the importance of sharing the book with Manson and others involved.
Donal Barty mentions signed copies are available at the Criminals Hall of Fame.
